errors.english: I maintain that agent and action are established dependently.
errors.why: gdags pa is 'designated' (prajñapti): agent and action are designated in dependence, not 'established', which is exactly what the Madhyamaka denies of them.

errors.english: would you not fall into the fault of asserting that things arise without a cause? Would all those criticisms not then apply to you?
errors.why: The opponent says the faults that YOU pointed out (e.g. 'it would follow that there is no cause') would now apply to you yourself; the English loses that they are the Madhyamika's own earlier criticisms turned back on him.

note: A careful rendering of Buddhapālita's six-alternative argument and the sesame simile; the key Madhyamaka term 'designated' is flattened to 'established'.
Faithful rendering of the commentary on beings being buddhas and the elements as the sisters; notes are unobtrusive.

errors.english: You cannot demonstrate that space is not a functioning entity.
errors.why: The opponent is citing the Madhyamika's claim that the thesis 'space is an entity' cannot be demonstrated; a negation has been added.

fix.find: You cannot demonstrate that space is not a functioning entity.
fix.replace: [You said:] "It cannot be demonstrated that space is a functioning entity."

errors.english: By stating these three reasons and examples, the opponent argues that the Madhyamaka cannot disprove that space is an entity.
errors.why: The Vaibhāṣika says: when I stated three reasons and examples, [you replied that] the thesis 'space is an entity' cannot be demonstrated; it is not the opponent arguing that the Madhyamika cannot disprove it.

fix.find: By stating these three reasons and examples, the opponent argues that the Madhyamaka cannot disprove that space is an entity.
fix.replace: When I stated these three reasons and examples, [you said that] the thesis that space is an entity cannot be demonstrated.

errors.english: your proof and the thing to be proven would simply fail
errors.why: The probandum and probans that fail are the opponent's (the speaker's) own, as the Madhyamika charged, not the Madhyamika's.

errors.english: space is merely the absence of obstructive contact
errors.why: The Tibetan says only that the Sautrāntikas hold space to be a non-entity; 'absence of obstructive contact' is an interpretive gloss put into the body of the text.

note: Avalokitavrata's framing of the Vaibhāṣika pūrvapakṣa is reversed twice, so the reader cannot follow who claims what about space.

errors.english: For wrathful activities, burn a corpse.
errors.why: In this list of pen materials the line names the stylus for abhicāra (a charred corpse/cremation-remains pen), not an instruction to burn a corpse.

errors.english: [note: The text continues with a commentary on the Vajravarahi Tantra]
errors.why: The clause identifies Vajravārāhī as the listener ('by me' etc.) of this tantra (the Ḍākārṇava, as the next side says); the text is not turning to a Vajravārāhī Tantra commentary.

note: The lists of ritual materials and the caṇḍālī verses are rendered clearly; one pen-material line and the closing note mislead.
Accurate rendering of the moon/sun channel and prāṇa/apāna correlations.

errors.english: so too the Buddhists argue that even if there is a difference, there are no distinct particulars
errors.why: This is the opponent's tu quoque against the Buddhist: just as [you object to] the Sāṃkhya, the same consequence holds for the Buddhist too, since things that are all equally different are without distinction; the Buddhists are not the ones arguing it.

fix.find: so too the Buddhists argue that even if there is a difference, there are no distinct particulars
fix.replace: so too the same consequence applies to the Buddhists: although things are different, there is no distinction among them in being different

errors.english: Who is the opponent making this challenge?
errors.why: The question is 'what is this rejoinder (counter-objection)?', which the commentary then explains with the rice-sprout example, not a question about who the opponent is.

note: The apoha exposition is mostly sound, but the closing objection is misattributed to the Buddhists, which inverts the dialectic.

errors.why: dGongs pa lung bstan is the Sandhivyākaraṇa Tantra (a Guhyasamāja explanatory tantra); 'Vyakarana-ashaya' is not its title.

note: The list of bhūmis and the bhaga etymology are rendered faithfully; one wrong title in a note.

errors.why: dbang po here is Indra: the image is Indra's banner (indradhvaja) that falls when the festival ends, not a 'crest of the senses'.

errors.english: it was out of joy, yet not without respect
errors.why: The verse says it was joy but not respect, the paradoxical mirror of the previous line; 'not without respect' inverts it.

fix.find: it was out of joy, yet not without respect
fix.replace: it was out of joy, yet not respect

note: A readable rendering of the Licchavis' lament, with Indra's banner lost and one paradoxical line inverted.

errors.english: there is no non-engagement; this is the fifth unshared quality.
errors.why: The Tibetan says the Tathāgata does not engage (in perceiving beings as different), the end of the fifth āveṇika dharma; 'no non-engagement' turns it into a positive.

note: Faithful account of the sixth to twelfth unshared qualities of a Buddha.

errors.english: the eight pillars of the (mandala) sacred circle
errors.why: 'khor lo la sogs pa is the eight pillars marked with the wheel and the other emblems, not the 'mandala' pillars.

errors.english: In these nineteen divine abodes, the darkness inherent in the continuums of all sentient beings is cleared away
errors.why: Clearing darkness, drying the mud of the ten non-virtues and ripening the bodhicitta sprout all describe the seven sun seats on the nineteen deity places; the English attaches the first two to the abodes.

note: Sound rendering of the eight liberations and Ānandagarbha's mandala symbolism, with minor mis-segmentation of the seat description.
